title: Prostitution-related arrests in New York State, by top arrest charge, statewide
geography: New York State, statewide. County-level counts for these Penal Law sections are not published openly; DCJS's open county dataset (data.ny.gov rikd-mt35) groups arrests into broad felony and misdemeanour categories only.
unit: arrest events, counted once under the most serious charge (DCJS fingerprintable arrests, adults 18 and older)

years_missing.2020-2022: no open offence-level series located; DCJS data request needed
years_missing.2019 loitering: the published table gives ten values for eleven years for PL 240.37; the 2019 value is left blank rather than guessed

groups.sold: Prostitution (PL 230.00) and loitering for prostitution (PL 240.37, repealed 2021): the women and people sold
groups.bought: Patronizing a person for prostitution, all degrees (PL 230.03, .04, .05, .06, .08) and aggravated patronizing a minor (PL 230.11): the buyers
groups.promoted: Promoting prostitution, all degrees (PL 230.19, .20, .25, .30, .32), compelling (PL 230.33) and permitting (PL 230.40): pimps and premises
groups.trafficked: Sex trafficking (PL 230.34) and child sex trafficking (PL 230.34-a)
groups.massage: Unauthorized practice of a profession (Education Law 6512), the charge used against unlicensed massage workers

sources.name: Decriminalize Sex Work, By the Numbers: New York's Treatment of Sex Workers and Trafficking Survivors (2022), Table 2, from a New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services data request
New York State Unified Court System, Human Trafficking Intervention Courts
Data Collaborative for Justice, Four Decades of Law Enforcement in New York, summary (Dec 2024), DCJS data

caution: A review is a selected post, not a count of buyers or offences. Do not divide arrests by reviews and call the result an impunity rate.
